# The Flight Plan and the group Course Design Project

|  |  |
|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
|  **Individual Flight Plan** |  **Group Course Design Project** |
| Your own locally grounded idea or aspiration. It may begin as a   wish, need or opportunity and should be close enough to your context that you   can speak with relevant people after the course. | A larger course or curriculum idea developed collaboratively   around a defined theme during the course. |
| Emphasises reflection, stakeholder engagement, evidence,   feasibility, revision and readiness for a future next step. | Emphasises collaborative course design, shared decisions,   educational structure and a collective output. |
| You submit your own work at three intervals and remain the owner   of the plan. |  The group develops and presents the work together under the   group-project brief. |

The projects may inform one another, but they do not need to use the same topic or produce the same output.

What belongs in each project:

#### Use the Individual Flight Plan when

· The idea comes from your own role, interests, institution or community.

· You need to explore a need or opportunity before deciding what response would help.

· You want to engage stakeholders and consider feasibility, permission or support.

· The eventual response might be a course, but it could instead become mentoring, a resource, a community activity or another intervention.

· You want to develop an idea that you may later propose to a manager, head of department, partner or funder.

#### Use the group Course Design Challenge when

· The group makes design decisions collaboratively.

· The intended output is a course, curriculum or structured learning experience.

· The purpose is to practise applying the course design process with others.

· The group will explain or present one collective design.

#### If the ideas overlap

You may reuse relevant learning, evidence or insights across the two projects. Do not submit the group output as your Individual Flight Plan. Your Flight Plan must show your own context, reasoning, engagement, decisions and next action.

A useful distinction is: the Course Design Challenge asks how the group can design a strong learning experience together. The Individual Flight Plan asks what idea you want to explore and advance in your own setting.
